latin_text: Πᾶσαν σχεδὸν τὴν γῆν διελθὼν, καὶ ἐπὶ πέντε καὶ τριάκοντα ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ διαθλεύσας ἐνιαυτοῖς. Niceph. hist. eccles. lib. 12. cap. 34. Vix triginta annorum spatio et Romanos, et Persas, et Parthos, et Medos, et Indos, et Scythas, et Sauromatas, et Sarracenos, et omne prorsus humanum genus sub jugum mitteret veritatis, &c. Chrysost. homil. 4. de laudib. Pauli. Clemens in epistola ad Corinthios pag. 8. de eodem: Κῆρυξ γενόμενος ἐν τῇ ἀνατολῇ καὶ ἐν τῇ δύσει, τὸ γενναῖον τῆς πίστεως αὑτοῦ κλέος ἔλαβεν δικαιοσύνην διδάξαι ὅλον τὸν κόσμον, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ τέρμα τῆς δύσεως ἐλθὼν, καὶ μαρτυρήσας ἐπὶ τῶν ἡγουμένων, οὕτως ἀπηλλάγη τοῦ κόσμου. In oriente ac occidente verbi præco factus, illustrem fidei suæ fainam sortitus est, in justitia mundum universum instruens, et ad occidentis terminos veniens, et sub imperatoribus martyrium subiens, sic e mundo migravit.

translation_history.english: Πᾶσαν σχεδὸν τὴν γῆν διελθὼν, καὶ ἐπὶ πέντε καὶ τριάκοντα ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ διαθλεύσας ἐνιαυτοῖς. Nicephorus, "Ecclesiastical History," book 12, chapter 34. "In a span of barely thirty years he would bring under the yoke of truth the Romans, Persians, Parthians, Medes, Indians, Scythians, Sarmatians, Saracens, and indeed the whole human race, etc." Chrysostom, Homily 4, "On the Praises of Paul." Clement, in the Epistle to the Corinthians, page 8, on the same: Κῆρυξ γενόμενος ἐν τῇ ἀνατολῇ καὶ ἐν τῇ δύσει, τὸ γενναῖον τῆς πίστεως αὑτοῦ κλέος ἔλαβεν δικαιοσύνην διδάξαι ὅλον τὸν κόσμον, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ τέρμα τῆς δύσεως ἐλθὼν, καὶ μαρτυρήσας ἐπὶ τῶν ἡγουμένων, οὕτως ἀπηλλάγη τοῦ κόσμου. "Having become a herald of the word in the East and the West, he obtained the illustrious fame of his faith, instructing the whole world in righteousness; and coming to the bounds of the West, and undergoing martyrdom under the rulers, thus he departed from the world."
translation_history.notes: Clement Greek preserved verbatim because immediately followed by Ussher's Latin paraphrase ('In oriente ac occidente …'), per Hard Rule 1. Nicephorus Greek also kept verbatim for editorial consistency (its substance is paraphrased in the body). Proper-noun normalization: Sauromatæ → Sarmatians, Sarraceni → Saracens (Rule 3). 'fainam' is a print/OCR artefact for 'famam' (fame) — translated as 'fame'. 'sub imperatoribus' rendered 'under the rulers' to match Greek ἡγουμένων.
